title.narrative: Livelihoods and Leadership: Tackling Gender Inequality and Sexual Violence in Conflict and Ebola Aff

description.narrative: Many women and girls in Liberia are not aware of their rights and live in an environment where domestic violence is often seen as the norm. Gender inequality and women's marginalization are entrenched in traditional and religious perceptions. The target region is home to three of Liberia's most patriarchal tribes (Lorma, Kpelle and Mandingo) and as a result, women and girls are often unable to equally participate in educational and economic life. Many women who may want to work are denied the freedom to choose by their family and even when women work, their income is often handed over to their husbands or another male member of the family to manage. Disadvantaged women and girls unable to provide for their basic needs resort to prostitution and survival sex and are at a higher risk of contracting HIV/AIDS and other sexually transmitted diseases. As a result of the current Ebola epidemic, women and girls in the target districts are becoming increasingly vulnerable to a variety of risks. For examples, women’s traditional role as caregivers to children, the sick and the elderly exposes them to disease, stigma, financial insecurity and extreme poverty. Levels of gender discrimination and violence against women and girls have increased in the fragile country and in addition to the lack of education, civil society actors including UN Women and Plan UK are reporting increased levels of child pregnancies and forced early marriages as parents struggle to support their daughters and often see it as the only solution.
